title: Parse it right or pay for it later
brief: Half of the corpus is clean exports, the rest is scans with merged-cell tables, forms and charts. One parser for everything is tempting. Pick by document type, volume and where the text may travel.

blocks.text: What the parser must hand over

blocks.md: Chunking cannot repair what parsing lost. A parser has to return reading order, tables with their structure, figures and, when you cite pages, coordinates. Topics `w03-t03` (extraction, OCR, layout), `w03-t04` (vision LLMs and Content Understanding) and `w03-t05` (tables, figures, forms) explain the mechanisms. Benchmarks agree that quality varies by document type [[r21]], and some systems skip text parsing and embed page images instead [[r22]]. Here you choose per document class.

blocks.title: Pick a parser for a document class
blocks.prompt: Flip the constraints. Real corpora need a different answer per class, so run the board once for each.

values.label: A managed cloud service is allowed

options.name: Native text extraction
options.summary: Read the text layer of born-digital files, with no model involved.

options.name: Layout analysis (Document Intelligence)
options.summary: A managed OCR and layout model that returns Markdown, tables, figures and coordinates.

options.name: Content Understanding
options.summary: Managed analyzers that extract and chunk in one skill, with schema-defined fields.

options.name: Open-source parser you run
options.summary: Docling or Unstructured with layout, tables and OCR, self-hosted.

options.name: Vision LLM reads each page
options.summary: Send page images to a multimodal model and ask for structured text.

clean.why: The text layer is already there, so extraction is fast, cheap and deterministic.

scans.why: A scan has no text layer, and flattened tables lose their structure.

visual.why: Charts and figures carry no extractable text, so their content is lost.

small.why: Cheap at any size, though a small volume does not need cheap.

huge.why: No per-page fee and no model throughput limit.

local.why: A local library keeps the text inside your network.

clean.why: Works, but you pay for a model that adds little to clean text.

scans.why: OCR, per-line handwriting flags and HTML tables with merged cells and multi-row headers, in Markdown output [[r15]].

visual.why: Figures come back with bounding regions, not a description of what they show [[r15]].

small.why: A per-page price is a small bill at this volume.

huge.why: Per-page cost and service limits add up (S0 allows 500 MB and 2,000 pages per file) [[r27]].

local.why: It is a cloud service. Confirm a deployment that keeps data in your network before assuming one.

clean.why: Works, but it is more machinery than clean text needs.

scans.why: Layout-aware extraction. The AI Search skill outputs tables as Markdown and lets chunks span pages [[r18]].

visual.why: Covers images, audio and video, and AI image descriptions exist, though they are preview [[r17]] [[r18]].

huge.why: Asynchronous document analysis is capped at 200 MB and 300 pages per PDF, so large files need splitting [[r28]].

cloud.why: API 2025-11-01 is GA, and the skill is GA in search REST 2026-04-01 [[r17]] [[r18]].

local.why: It is a managed cloud service, so text leaves your network.

clean.why: Reads PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and HTML without a service call [[r19]].

scans.why: Docling covers layout, reading order, tables, code, formulas and OCR for scans [[r19]].

visual.why: Finding a figure is not describing it. A chart description needs a vision model on top.

small.why: You run and patch the service even for a small job.

huge.why: No per-page fee, so cost is compute and operations, which you can scale.

cloud.why: Allowed, but not a reason to pick it.

local.why: It can run locally for sensitive or air-gapped data. The Docling code is MIT licensed, and model licences vary [[r19]].

clean.why: Slower and costlier than reading the text layer, and the output can drift between runs.

scans.why: Reads messy layouts well, but can drop or invent cells, so every table needs validation.

visual.why: The one option here that can read a chart or diagram and say what it shows.

small.why: Token cost per page is tolerable at small volume.

huge.why: Token cost per page and model throughput dominate at this volume.

local.why: Only a self-hosted vision model qualifies, which adds GPU operations.

blocks.takeaway: No parser wins every class. Route by document type: native text for clean files, layout analysis or a local parser for scans and tables, and a vision model only for the pages whose meaning is a picture.

blocks.caption: Keep tables, figures and forms answerable
head: Content
Representation
Wins when
Loses when
rows: Table
Whole table as HTML or Markdown in one chunk, with its caption
It fits in a chunk and questions need several rows
A large table splits mid-row or exceeds the embedding input limit
Table
One chunk per row, with the header repeated in each
Questions look up one row, such as a price or a limit
Questions compare many rows, and the index grows by the row count
Table
A short LLM summary embedded, raw table kept in the payload
Natural-language questions about a dense numeric table
The summary drops a number, so the raw table must reach the model
Figure
Caption plus a vision-model description as its own chunk, with the image URL
The answer lives in a chart or diagram
The description is a model guess. If it splits across chunks, repeat the image URL in each chunk [[r35]]
Form
Extract named fields into a schema and store them as metadata
Questions ask for a field, such as an invoice total
Layouts vary so much that field confidence is low, so route those to review [[r17]]

items.symptom: Checkbox and table parsing code broke after an upgrade to layout v4.0
items.cause: v4.0 (2024-11-30) renders tables as HTML and selection marks as the characters ☒ and ☐, instead of `:selected:` and `:unselected:` [[r15]].
items.fix: Parse the new forms and keep a regression set of tricky pages that runs on every parser upgrade.

items.symptom: Big PDFs fail in the Document Layout skill yet still show on the bill
items.cause: Documents needing over 5 minutes in the layout model time out, and are still charged when a Foundry resource is attached [[r16]].
items.fix: Split very large files into page ranges before ingest, or route them through a separate batch path.

items.symptom: Answers quote the wrong number from a table
items.cause: A merged-cell or multi-row header was flattened, or a vision model dropped a cell.
items.fix: Score tables against a labelled set per document type, and keep the raw table so the model reads cells instead of a summary.

items.symptom: Every document re-embeds after a parser upgrade
items.cause: Open-source parsers release often (Docling v2.138.0 on 2026-10-12, Unstructured 0.27.25 on 2026-10-10) and the output shifts [[r19]] [[r20]].
items.fix: Pin versions, run the regression set before upgrading, and include the parser version in the re-embedding key beside the content hash.

blocks.title: Where the docs disagree, as of 2026-10-13
blocks.md: The Content Understanding skill page says it outputs tables and figures as Markdown and that the Document Layout skill gives plain text, while the Document Layout skill page lists `markdown` as its default `outputFormat` [[r16]] [[r18]]. Test both on your own tables. Semantic chunking in the Content Understanding skill and AI image descriptions are preview (`2026-05-01-preview`), and API `2026-06-01-preview` adds signature detection and document metadata extraction [[r17]] [[r18]].

quiz.q: Questions about a merged-cell price table return wrong numbers. The pipeline extracts the text layer and splits recursively, and the chunks read cleanly. What do you change first?
options: Switch to a parser that keeps table structure, then re-test the table questions
Raise top-k from 5 to 20 so that more of the table's rows are retrieved per query
Move to a larger embedding model so that numbers and units embed more precisely
Increase the chunk overlap so that each row of the table appears in two chunks
quiz.explain: Text-layer extraction flattens merged cells and multi-row headers before any chunker sees them, so the numbers already lost their column. Layout analysis returns tables as HTML with merged cells preserved [[r15]]. A higher top-k, a bigger embedding model and more overlap all operate on the flattened text and cannot restore the structure.

quiz.q: You propose sending every page of a 100-million-page archive to a vision LLM. Select the costs a reviewer should raise.
options: Token cost per page scales with volume and dominates the bill
Output is not deterministic, so a re-run or model update can change the chunks
It can never run inside a private network, even with a self-hosted model
Cells can be dropped or invented, so tables need validation against a labelled set
quiz.explain: Per-page token cost, non-deterministic output and silent cell errors are the real costs, and they push you to route only visual pages to the model. A self-hosted vision model can run on a private network, at the price of GPU operations, so the third option overstates the limit.

quiz.q: Match each parsing component to the fact most likely to bite you.

pairs.r: Times out when a document needs over 5 minutes in the layout model
Tables as HTML and selection marks as ☒ and ☐
GA in search REST 2026-04-01, extracts and chunks in one skill
MIT-licensed code that can run locally on air-gapped data

quiz.explain: Each pairing is a documented constraint you would plan around: the skill timeout and billing [[r16]], the v4.0 output change that breaks old parsers [[r15]], the single extract-and-chunk skill [[r18]] and the local, MIT-licensed option [[r19]].

takeaways: Chunking cannot repair what parsing lost, so test tables and figures before you tune chunk size
Route by document class: native text, layout analysis or a local parser, and a vision model only where the picture is the content
Name the version and status: layout v4.0 changed table and checkbox output, and Content Understanding semantic chunking is preview
Keep a regression set of hard pages and re-run it on every parser upgrade
